source.title: Context Awareness: Constitutional AI can mitigate Emergent Misalignement

record.file_problem: None; the full post text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether narrow harmful fine-tuning produces out-of-domain misalignment and whether prior character training changes that outcome, using a judge-scored alignment measure and additional training domains and models.
record.gate_note: The post reports its own EM fine-tuning results, including an insecure-code condition, other harmful training domains, character-trained conditions, and contextualized reflection. Results cited from other studies, including the secure-code and educational-insecure controls from Betley et al., are not recorded as rows. No numerical outcomes are stated for several personas beyond ranges or qualitative descriptions; those are recorded only at the level reported.
record.test_reason: The post reports its own EM fine-tunes of Qwen 2.5 7B and Llama 3.1 8B. It covers insecure code and three narrow bad-advice datasets (Turner et al.), with judge-scored misalignment on the 8 general questions. These results bear directly on V1, V2 and V7. Most of the post studies prior character training as protection, which is not one of the V6 interventions.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Constitutional-AI character training mitigates EM: every Qwen persona reduces critical misalignment, and most Llama personas are strongly protective. Exceptions are model-dependent (Llama sarcasm). Goodness-Meta-V2 does best. Contextualized reflection gives moderate, lesser protection. Their Bateson 'logical type discrimination' account is offered as a hypothesis, not a proven mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the Model Organisms for EM LoRA fine-tuning protocol and general-question evaluations, but adds prior Constitutional AI persona training, custom constitutions, other harmful training domains, and GPT-4.1-mini alignment scoring with critical-rate thresholds. It does not reproduce the original study's matched secure-code and educational-insecure control experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies by base model (Qwen versus Llama), persona, and EM training domain. The post reports a Qwen/Llama reversal for sarcasm, domain-specific reversals for Mathematical and Nonchalance on Qwen, and different outcomes for Goodness-Meta variants versus pure Metacommunication. The reflection results are shown across training checkpoints.

fits_no_version.finding: Prior Constitutional-AI character training, of almost any persona, lowers post-EM critical misalignment on Qwen. The effect is model-dependent: sarcasm is harmful on Llama.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prior character training reduces susceptibility to emergent misalignment, with persona- and model-dependent exceptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Appending the pre-corruption model's self-reflection to each corrupted sample attenuates the alignment drop (~75–80 vs ~50).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contextualized self-reflection augmentation of harmful fine-tuning data partially mitigates emergent misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: On a direction taken from the baseline's pre- to post-EM activation shift, the Goodness model's projection rises more slowly and plateaus lower across all layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Character training slows internal movement along the EM activation direction during fine-tuning.

record.problems: The post relies primarily on a single judge, GPT-4.1-mini, and describes its alignment score as coarse; it notes that covertly harmful outputs may be under-scored as misaligned. Original persona conditions have about 400 responses per condition, while custom constitutional variants have about 80 or 240 in the reported comparisons, with wider intervals. Only two base-model architectures are tested; Llama is evaluated on only 4 of 8 evaluation datasets and its misalignment persona was not generated. No seed robustness is reported. The authors state that the DPO and SFT contributions of the character-training pipeline cannot be disentangled, and acknowledge the absence of neutral-data or arbitrary-LoRA controls for the possibility that any extra fine-tuning creates inertia. They also report one evaluation question overlapping semantically with risky-financial training and say the theoretical mechanism is not proven.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately quantified main-condition persona rates are stated in the text beyond the reported aggregate range and the named results. Approximate domain-level values for selected other meta-personas are included only where stated; plot-only values without a textual description were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Matched secure-code and educational-insecure controls are not run; they are only cited from Betley et al. No pre-fine-tune rate is reported. No Llama insecure-code result is reported.
Entire version; the authors list RL-induced EM as out of scope.
Whether one direction mediates EM across fine-tunes. The direction is taken from one baseline trajectory only, with no cross-dataset or causal test.
Inoculation prompting and brief benign re-training are not tested. Character training and reflection are different interventions.
Seed robustness, coherence-filtered rates, and model-size scaling.

record.verdict_notes: The Quick Tour wrongly describes training on insecure code and evaluating on financial, medical and sports questions. The Methods say each model is trained separately on each of 4 datasets and evaluated on 8 general questions; the rows correctly follow the latter. The reader had set persona-row states from the protection perspective; these were re-stated as EM presence for V2. There is no neutral-LoRA control, so an 'any extra fine-tuning' explanation of the protection remains open. Single judge (GPT-4.1-mini); the commenter notes Goodness-Meta-V2's lead is not statistically significant. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test matched secure-code or educational-insecure controls; those results are cited from Betley et al. It also does not report the unmodified base model's neutral-prompt rate separately from the EM-fine-tuned baseline.
Tests bad medical, risky financial, and extreme-sports training domains, but not reward hacks or number sequences.
No narrow in-context-only intervention is tested.

Measures projections onto a direction derived from the baseline trajectory for a baseline and Goodness condition, but does not test whether one direction or persona feature mediates the behavior across fine-tunes.
Does not test inoculation prompting or brief benign re-training. Contextualized reflection is a distinct data augmentation, not one of the interventions specified in this version.

Compares Qwen 2.5 7B and Llama 3.1 8B, reports effect sizes and some training curves, but does not test seed robustness or coherence-filtered results. Training-stage curves are reported for the reflection experiment, not the main character-training comparison.
